name: Thyroid Carcinoma and the Bethesda Cytopathology System

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / American Thyroid Association Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Bethesda classification: I non-diagnostic, II benign (<3% risk), III AUS/FLUS, IV follicular neoplasm (25-40%), V suspicious, VI malignant (97-99%)
Papillary thyroid cancer (85% of cases): Orphan Annie eye nuclei, nuclear pseudoinclusions, psammoma bodies; lymphatic spread; >95% survival
Follicular thyroid cancer: FNA cannot distinguish from adenoma; requires histological proof of capsular or vascular invasion; hematogenous spread
Medullary thyroid cancer arises from calcitonin-secreting parafollicular C cells; associated with RET mutations in MEN 2A and 2B
Thyroidectomy complications: hypoparathyroidism (hypocalcemia, Chvostek/Trousseau signs), recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy (hoarseness), hematoma
reference.pathophysiology: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is driven by BRAF V600E mutations (60%) or RET/PTC translocations, activating the MAPK pathway. Follicular carcinoma is driven by RAS mutations or PAX8-PPARG fusions. Anaplastic carcinoma represents undifferentiated transformation with TP53 mutations, presenting as a rapidly expanding, highly lethal neck mass invading tracheal and esophageal structures.
additionalDifferentials: Follicular thyroid carcinoma vs follicular adenoma
additionalInvestigations: Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (FNA) with Bethesda reporting
Serum calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) for medullary carcinoma
